title: Design and deliver independent CI for every project
body: Operator priority: build one reliable CI platform for the operator's projects, independent of GitHub Actions. This is a delivery outcome, not another comparison that ends by asking whether to use Proxmox.

Operator instructions, verbatim:
- "Nie wiem szperaj szerzej, moze cos jeszcze lepszego znadjziesz, czy to juz jest absolutnie najlepsza opcja?"
- "No na spokojnie, przebudujemy wszystko, to jest chuj a nie koszt migracji bo w chuj ułatwi nam życie w przyszłości."
- "No ale to kurwa napiszesz ten handoff / task zeby zaprojetkować zajebisty CI który wypierdoli ten zajebany github i wszystko i ogarnie wszystkie moje projekty żeby w koncu działały akcje jak nalezy? chcemy w końcu to skonfigurować jak senior devopsi i się już nie kopać z takim syfem............"

Outcome
Design, independently verify, qualify and deliver shared CI with an execution/control plane outside GitHub Actions. Prefer future reliability, isolation and low operational work over preserving the current KRN implementation. Rewriting deliver/admission, workflow configuration and required-check bindings is acceptable. A vendor-neutral source/GitHub integration must not make GitHub Actions the scheduler or the required producer. Treat removal of GitHub as the source-code host as an explicit design option, not an implicit authorization to move repositories.

Scope and next owner
A fresh lead owns the CI programme; the present lead focuses on Codex hooks. Read .krn/runs/delivery-loop/ci-infrastructure/handoff.md, operator-direction.md and research_notes/CI infrastruktura porównanie możliwości/. Existing reports/pilot are research until marked reviewed; do not execute an obsolete GHA-first pilot. Inventory all operator-owned project CI needs before promising universal coverage. Start with Product and GLOBAL receivers, then a materially different project such as mise-en-plesk, then onboard the remaining inventory in bounded changes. Preserve each repository's workflow and dirty-state ownership; do not impose KRN on repositories that have not adopted it.

Required design and independent review
Choose and justify the target architecture from native managed CI/full-VM executors and a mature self-managed alternative. Compare practical Linux capabilities, scheduling and outage independence, resource isolation, ongoing patching/backup/recovery work, observable failures and total cost. Existing PVE/Hyper-V inventory is evidence, not a granted resource budget. Nested KVM and dedicated physical hardware are not requirements derived from the current gate. Obtain independent review of the proposed architecture and concrete rollout before infrastructure changes; self-assessment is not acceptance.

Observable acceptance
1. A project catalogue records repository/owner, current trigger and gate, toolchain pins, platform requirements, secrets scope and migration order. Coverage is measured against that catalogue.
2. An adopted architecture and executable pilot prove a fresh, isolated full Linux environment, user namespaces/bwrap and systemd --user for KRN, bounded resources/concurrency, cancellation, cleanup after failure and durable diagnostic logs. No weakening tests, blanket retries or isolation skips to make a provider pass.
3. A real pilot schedules and runs while GitHub Actions is disabled or unused. Distinguish independence from Actions billing from availability of a GitHub-hosted source repository/API. No unverified claim that self-hosted GHA bypasses account billing locks.
4. Product and GLOBAL full gates pass on exact source SHAs. Record job-level results, zero isolation skips, logs and actual durations. Product's observed baseline is 2 vCPU/8 GB, median 407.5 s from four jobs; GLOBAL runs two tiers, median combined 1041 s. P95 and provider qualification remain unmeasured until tested.
5. KRN deliver/admission/ship and repository policies consume the chosen CI's genuine exact-head evidence with explicit trusted producer identity. Remove hardcoded github-actions/gate assumptions through reviewed changes; never fabricate a GitHub Actions success or silently bypass admission. Describe the one-time bootstrap explicitly.
6. Product, GLOBAL and a distinct project are onboarded end to end; remaining projects follow the catalogue with owners and clear completion status. Reusable templates preserve repository-specific commands and permissions.
7. Infrastructure/configuration has a durable reviewed owner, exact tool/image pins, scoped credentials outside workers, health/queue visibility, documented update/recovery procedures and a tested shutdown/rollback path. The operator receives a usable platform and runbook, not an unmaintained custom scheduler.
8. Retire old CI/fleet only after receiver-boundary proof and explicit cutover. Parked Product PR #144 at 610624b and its claim remain intact until its real required CI can complete.

Authority
The operator explicitly prioritizes broad CI redesign and accepts code migration cost. Existing read-only grants remain in force. This task is not a grant for credentials/new accounts or GitHub Apps, purchases, install/seal, production hosts/network/backups, repository moves, ruleset changes or cutover. Prepare the concrete candidate, pilot, effects, cost ceiling and rollback first; request only the exact missing grant, never repeat a recorded one. Do not spawn a background lead automatically.

Evidence and cautions
- Existing host evidence: .krn/runs/delivery-loop/ci-infrastructure/hosting-inventory.md; fresh receipts beside it.
- Research requirements/compute/managed and native-ci/owned-ci supplements: research_notes/CI infrastruktura porównanie możliwości/.
- PBS policy was updated in the hosting register after the initial inventory; preserve measurements and apply the later correction. Do not plan from old keep-all assumptions.
- Codex hook work is separate: .krn/runs/delivery-loop/codex-context/ and CI folder codex-context-audit.md. Its existence does not assign CI implementation to the hook lead.
